note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect is derived by hand from the printed 40-wire topology and the p.58 rule, not printed. The errata sheet has no Fortune Teller entry, so wires = as_printed = programs.json wiresCorrected/wiresEffective. Topology: relays 1-4 have their indicator side on minus (1E/2E/3C/4C/5C/6C/6-). Pushbutton 2 (2Y+, 2X/2F) drives relay 2 directly; relay 2's N.O. contacts put + on the set-2 arms of relays 5 (2K/5L) and 6 (2G/6L). Relay 5 at rest feeds 6E (5N/6E), operated feeds 6F (5K/6F); relay 6 at rest feeds 5F (6N/5F), operated feeds 5E (6K/5E). Each of relays 5 and 6 self-holds through set 1 (5H+/5G/5F, 6H+/6G/6F), so while pushbutton 2 is held the pair steps (5,6) = 00, 10, 11, 01, 00 ... by pulling in from F and being shunted (+ on both coil ends) from E: a four-state ring [likely, topology; p.59 'Push pushbutton 2 to allow MINIVAC to generate a random number.']. Relay 3's coil hangs on 5F (3F/5G), relay 4's on 6F (4F/6G), so on release relays 3 and 4 copy the latched 5 and 6. Pushbutton 4 (4Y+, 4X/4L) then feeds a two-level tree: relay 4 set 2 (4K/3H operated, 4N/3L at rest) then relay 3 (3H: 3G light 1 / 3J light 3; 3L: 3K light 2 / 3N light 4), so exactly one answer light lights while pushbutton 4 is held. Which one depends on the ring's phase at the pb2 release and is not printed (programs.json printedUnprinted; Step 7 notes: relay 6 drop-out margin 0 uA, phase-dependent under the robustness perturbations), so no expect names it. Checked instead: the cold rest state, the power-on answer before any contemplation (light 4, both answer relays at rest), relay 2 operated with answer lights dark during the hold, and answer lights dark with relay 2 at rest once both buttons are up. The 3000 ms hold, the 300 ms lamp-warm advances and releasing pushbutton 4 are script choices; pushbutton 2 is held with advance, not settle, because the ring does not settle. The page gives no reset; a second question re-drives the ring from its latched state.
